A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReTabSyn and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original Appendices A-I can be matched across versions; v2 adds Appendices J-O. The material supports a full comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream utility, fidelity, privacy, ablation, constraint-satisfaction, and regression experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds backbone comparisons, alternative-target evaluations, full-data experiments, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated target-perturbation probability from 0.7 to 0.5. This reconciles the sampling rule with the 50/50 default already described in v1 Section 4.7; it does not establish that experiments were rerun. The augmentation procedure, base framework, and DPO-Positive objective otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix M adds 12 alternative prediction targets across Churn, Obesity, Titanic, and Indian Liver Patient, substantially extending evaluation beyond each dataset's alignment target. Table 2 also adds Shoppers to the 1% prevalence evaluation. These expand task and scenario coverage within the retained datasets.

E2.justification: The original six generator baselines remain. Table 15 adds comparisons with prompted GPT-5.4 and a pretraining-only Qwen3.5 control on Wilt and Churn. This is a bounded expansion of the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include Qwen3.5-2B evaluation, alternative-target macro-OVR AUROC averaged over five classifiers, full-data Adult and Magic experiments in synthetic-only and augmented settings, and beta/lambda sweeps. These substantially extend the experimental design. The original Section 4.1 split, small-data size grid, and synthetic sample count remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices L, M, and O add tests of backbone dependence, transfer beyond the alignment target, and sensitivity to DPO temperature and regularization. Table 22 specifically tests removing the regularizer. These address substantial additional robustness and mechanism questions; the original Table 6 ablations and Figure 5 analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 2-5 gain standard errors across utility, fidelity, and privacy results, and Appendix K supplies small-data standard errors. New backbone and full-data tables report standard deviations. v1 already specified 10 random seeds, so this establishes expanded uncertainty reporting, not an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: New results include Shoppers PR-AUC of 0.670 for ReTabSyn versus 0.649 for SMOTE, backbone comparisons, eight wins among 12 alternative targets, full-data results, and sensitivity outcomes. Table 3 changes TVAE's Liver AUC from 0.563 to 0.565. Most retained table means are unchanged. Newly tabulated small-data means in Table 14 do not fully agree with the retained Figure 3.

T1.justification: The utility-gap definition, attributed utility bound, assumptions, and optimization objective remain mathematically unchanged. New equations for perturbations and autoregressive factorization formalize previously described procedures. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain the same claims about oracle-free preference construction, conditional alignment, and utility in difficult data regimes. The conclusion retains the same central contribution. Additional validation and qualifications do not redefine the core proposal.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies ReTabSyn as target-aware rather than fully task-agnostic and explains regression weakness through its discrete-label perturbation design. Section 3.3 clarifies feature perturbation as regularization rather than estimation of P(A|B). New backbone, target-transfer, and sensitivity results receive substantive mechanism and applicability interpretations, extending the discussion beyond v1.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. v2 adds dataset eligibility criteria and an audit, specifies the new model identifiers, and clarifies that interpolated training rows are excluded from downstream evaluation. Existing hardware, runtime, and baseline implementation details are retained. Repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against oracle-guided tabular methods remain the same. GReaT, TabSyn, and AutoDiff references receive publication metadata updates. The explicit statement that Theorem 1 belongs to Xu et al. reinforces attribution already present in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted method and results rewrites, expands explanations, and adds limitations, funding disclosures, and appendix sections. The original section sequence and most existing prose remain, so the language and narrative changes are limited rather than a wholesale reorganization.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 expand from single-column to full-width displays, Tables 2-5 gain uncertainty formatting and revised captions, and Appendices J-O add Tables 13-22. This substantially expands and reorganizes the tabular presentation. All five original figures are retained, with some relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence about backbone dependence, target transfer, and regularization, supplies previously missing uncertainty, and states limitations more clearly. However, new reporting inconsistencies limit these gains: Section 4.3 claims non-overlapping Adult standard-error intervals although 0.906 ± 0.013 and 0.891 ± 0.010 overlap. Table 14 also places ReTabSyn below real-data training at 64 rows, contrary to the unchanged Figure 3(a). The broader assessment supports a limited net improvement, but central result reporting remains insufficiently reconciled.
